title: Nasal swab machine learning classifier estimates lung cancer probability in nodules
summary: A machine learning classifier using whole-transcriptome sequencing of nasal epithelial cells and clinical factors was trained on 1120 patients with nodules up to 30 mm and validated on an independent set of 312 patients. Low-risk classification had sensitivity 96% and specificity 42%, and high-risk classification had sensitivity 58% and specificity 90%, comparing favorably with clinical-only models.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifier on nasal epithelial transcriptome and clinical features
organization: Lahey Hospital and Medical Center; Lahey Medical Center

evidence.tested: Independent validation set of 312 patients with outcomes from final diagnosis or 12-month surveillance.
evidence.unknown: Moderate specificity at low risk; limited to smokers and former smokers with small nodules; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning combines gene expression and clinical factors into risk categories.
